_comment: What an Open5GS core cannot know: the radio, and where it is. Copy to cells.json and set OPEN5GS_CELLS_PATH. Cell identity, which UEs are attached and session state all come live from the core - nothing here repeats them.
_on_open5g2go: If you set OPEN5G2GO_URL, most of this file is unnecessary: that backend reads band, EARFCN, bandwidth, TX power, PRB utilisation and the radio's real MAC/serial/model/firmware over SNMP, and live values always beat declared ones. A whole inventory can then be one entry with a model and a placement - see docs/OPEN5GS.md.
_site_id: Which UniFi site the cells belong to; decides which floor plans they can sit on. Leave empty on a single-site console and the first site polled is used. OPEN5GS_SITE_ID overrides this.
_network_name: Shown as the client's network, where a Wi-Fi client would show an SSID. Falls back to the DNN, then the PLMN.

cells._comment: A cell matched by the gNB id it announces over NG. Find it in GET /api/cellular, or curl http://<amf>:9090/gnb-info. Every key in 'match' is looked up on the cell record VERBATIM, so it must be a field that record actually has - 'serial', not 'serial_number'; 'gnb_id', not 'gnbId'. A key nothing reports can never match, and what you get is this entry shown offline with its name, model and placement while the real cell sits beside it unnamed and unplaced. The log names the key and lists the available ones.
cells.name: CBRS Cell - Warehouse
cells._model: What this reports as its hardware. Hamina's Catalyst connector resolves models against Cisco hardware only, so for a Hamina import this must be a Cisco AP model - see docs/OPEN5GS.md. It is a costume, and the coverage simulation runs on that model's antenna pattern, not your cell's.

radio._comment: The RAN's own configuration. The core has never seen the radio, so these are the numbers from your gNB config - srsRAN, Amarisoft, or the small cell's own UI.
radio._wifi_channel: Optional. The Wi-Fi channel this cell reports to anything that only understands Wi-Fi. Left out, it is picked from the DFS range and stays put. There is no honest n48-to-Wi-Fi channel; this only has to be stable and out of the way.

placement._comment: Name a UniFi device that is already placed on the console's floor plan and the cell rides on its position - drag the anchor in UniFi and the cell moves, with nothing to edit here and nothing to re-import.
placement._dx_px: How far off the anchor to draw the cell, in floor-plan pixels. Left out it is nudged 24px so the two do not stack into one icon; set both to 0 to make them coincident.

cells._comment: A 4G cell, placed by hand instead of anchored. floorplan is an id from GET /api/floorplans; x_px/y_px are pixels on that plan's image - click them out at /sensors.
cells.name: LTE Cell - Yard

cells._comment: A cell placed in HAMINA rather than in UniFi. With PLAN_SOURCE=openintent the floor plan comes from a Hamina OpenIntent export, so anything you can draw on that plan gets a position - including a radio UniFi has never heard of and can never place. Draw the cell on the Hamina plan as an access point, name it, re-export, and name it here. It is reported at startup: any plan AP matching no live UniFi device is logged, and those names are exactly what anchor_ap accepts. No offset is applied to a plan-only anchor - it draws no icon of its own, so the cell sits exactly where you put it.
cells.name: CBRS Cell - Loading Dock

cells._comment: A spec with no 'match' is the fallback for any cell nothing else claimed - which is what a one-cell proof of concept wants: declare the radio once and it applies whatever gNB id turns up. A cell matched explicitly above always wins over this, whatever the file order. A fallback deliberately does NOT rename the cells it catches: it describes the radio, not its identity, so each keeps the name its own source gave it.
